To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the secreted paracrine factor from tumor cells induce molecular changes in MSC and these changes are tumor-specific.
paracrine factors of human glioblastoma and melanoma cells differently changed molecular characteristics of MSC, which explains their dual role in tumor growth.

paracrine factors secreted by melanoma cells induce differentiation of human MSC towards tumor-associated fibroblast phenotype, while glioblastoma-derived cytokines promote differentiation of MSC towards the progenitor phenotype, which is associated with the tumor-promoting effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular changes in the phenotype of MSC induced by tumor-derived paracrine factors and the functional consequences of these changes.
the molecular changes induced by tumor paracrine factors in MSC.
the mechanisms of tumor-stimulatory and tumor-inhibitory effects mediated by the paracrine factors in the MSC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MSC are a heterogeneous population of cells that can be differentiated into various phenotypes.
the MSC phenotype changes in response to the tumor-derived cytokines and the outcome of the tumor-stromal interaction is dictated by tumor-specific activating signals.
the paracrine factors secreted by the tumor cells can induce changes in MSC phenotype, which can affect the tumor growth.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
paracrine factors released by tumor cells can change MSC phenotype in vitro and in vivo.
the MSC are plastic in nature and are influenced by the microenvironment.
the tumor-derived paracrine factors induce the phenotypic changes in MSC and the tumor-specific paracrine stimulation determines the tumor-stimulatory and tumor-inhibitory effects of the MSC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor-derived factors can alter the MSC phenotype and their functional characteristics.
tumor-secreted factors can change MSC phenotype and their behavior, which can be exploited to design the MSC-based therapy.
the paracrine factors released by the tumor cells can induce changes in MSC phenotype.
